metadata.title: 50 States + District of Columbia Medicaid Casualty / TPL Reporting Directory
metadata.status: 51 PI / 51 WC state-program notification routes confirmed; 165 source-derived qualifications and 44 attributed user confirmations. Remaining notice requirements, plan allocation and downstream transactions are tracked separately.
methodology: Official state and identified contractor sources prioritized; secondary sources retained only as leads.
PI and WC initial-reporting statuses are independent. Plan-specific routes are separate from state/FFS routes.
An existing-case portal, general TPL contact, member/provider portal, estate process or contract award does not establish attorney new-case reporting.
Public-link observations are limited to available browser responses. JavaScript shells, blocked pages and logins were not transaction-tested.
No account was created, no form submitted, no client data transmitted and no telephone/email confirmation obtained.
Targeted second-pass checks were performed, but government procurement and every MCO were not exhaustively researched.
A reviewed date is not a website revision date or proof that an unresolved procedure is verified.
Unknown fields are null with UNRESOLVED status; omission never means no requirement.

status_definitions.VERIFIED — PRIMARY: Current primary source expressly supports the stated proposition; it does not certify end-to-end transaction success.
status_definitions.VERIFIED — CONTRACTOR: Identified contractor source expressly supports the proposition.
status_definitions.CORROBORATED: Multiple credible sources support the proposition, but current first-party operational instructions are absent.
status_definitions.MANUAL VERIFICATION REQUIRED: Specific issue or contact requires agency/contractor confirmation before reliance.

metadata.safety_note: Confirm recipient identity and an approved secure transmission method before sending PHI. Use the actual demand for case-specific payment instructions; no payment or client submission was made.

route_audit.coverage_meaning: Coverage includes exact primary/contractor-supported methods and explicitly attributed user-reviewed confirmations. Historical strict audit counts predate later manual corrections.

public_release.scope: Canonical bundled research only; no hosted database edits, reviews or case records.
public_release.currency: Snapshot date is packaging date, not fresh verification of every fact. Preserve per-fact verified_on and per-source reviewed_on dates. Legacy metadata.as_of and edition identify the earlier research baseline.

entity_to_notify.value: HMS Idaho Casualty / Gainwell
entity_to_notify.note: User-approved promotion on November 8, 2026 following the eight-state PI/WC parity review. Use the established PI casualty/TPL notification route for WC medical-cost recovery within the same payer/local scope. No affirmative evidence of a separate WC notification recipient, mechanism or exclusion was identified. This is an attributed user-confirmed parity decision, not a claim that every agency expressly states identical PI/WC procedures. Current IDAPA 16.03.26.026.08 applies subrogation and notice when a participant can recover medical expenses from any third party. The July 1, 2026 text does not divide notice by tort versus WC. Applying that notice framework to WC is a reasoned scope inference, supported by the federal inclusion of WC. Notification parity only. Published notice contents, triggers and attachments remain applicable. Disclosure authority, case-opening completion, itemized/interim/final claims, settlement, payment and managed-care/local allocation remain separately scoped. Department notice and contractor routing are combined explicitly; no new WC-only form or channel test is claimed.

mco_involvement.value: Illinois model contract section 9.1.39 permits MCO injury subrogation; current Molina Illinois Medicaid instructions specifically direct injury-liability referrals to Katch IQ: submitreferrals@katchiq.com. Identify separately paid HFS and other-plan interests; the HFS state recovery office is not blanket plan clearance. General plan inquiry routes: Use ABHILProviderRelations@aetna.com or 866-329-4701 to request plan-side assistance and the assigned casualty handler when no vendor file is known. The April 2026 notice supplies provider TPL assistance, not an express attorney casualty filing instruction. Optum is documented handling an Aetna Illinois lien in the cited court case;  its POBox 182643ColumbusOH 43218 is that record’s lien-payment address. Call 877-860-2837 for BCCHP plan/TPL inquiry and request routing for an injury-recovery matter. The published article concerns provider other-insurance validation and claim disputes;  it does not establish this as a dedicated casualty unit or confirm the parent 800-582-6418 line for Medicaid. Contact countycareproviderservices@cookcountyhhs.org or 312-864-8200,option 3, and request the CountyCare TPL/Finance recovery handler. The October 2026 guide confirms shared provider inquiry contacts;  attorney casualty service and a dedicated subrogation endpoint remain to be established. Do not equate CountyCare plan recovery with a CCH hospital lien. Call Meridian Medicaid 866-606-3700 to identify the assigned subrogation handler;  its official page directs legal matters to Attn:Legal,CentenePlaza,7700ForsythBoulevard,StLouisMO 63105. Rawlings and First Recovery Group are named in the Medicaid payment-code crosswalk;  the court record documents Meridian Medicaid liens with Equian/Rawlings. Confirm the current file’s handler rather than assigning all cases to one vendor. Use ILYouthCare@centene.com or 844-289-2264 for program-specific inquiry and request its casualty-recovery handler. Keep YouthCare identity separate from standard Meridian;  provider claim payerID instructions do not establish attorney notice requirements. DCFS.HealthPlan@illinois.gov/800-232-3798 is coverage/advocacy coordination, not a verified subrogation desk.

Disclosure authority, case-opening completion, itemized/interim/final claims, settlement, payment and managed-care/local allocation remain separately scoped. mco_involvement.value: Managed-care plans pursue casualty/tort recovery for their paid claims, including WC, under contract section 2.24.3. Home State Health expressly directs injury/WC reporting to 855-694-4663. Identify separate MO HealthNet state-paid claims; state Cost Recovery contact alone does not establish satisfaction of every plan interest. Call 877-236-1020 for WC, pending PI/tort/product-liability/medical-malpractice or auto matters. The 2026 subrogation section explicitly gives this specialty-program number; do not substitute Home State Health’s other-plan number. Call 866-292-0359 to report an injury/accident matter, including work injury, legal representation or accident recovery. The MO HealthNet handbook specifically gives the number in injury and subrogation instructions; request the assigned recovery handler. Report work/car accidents and pending PI/tort/product-liability/medical-malpractice matters to Healthy Blue at 833-388-1407 and notify FSD as the Medicaid handbook instructs. The separate 800-877-6876 accident-questionnaire line is an existing-questionnaire contact, not this initial reporting route.
mco_involvement.note: Allocation and named published contacts are established within the stated scope. Remaining plan endpoints and case-specific follow-through are tracked below; this is not blanket state completion.

entity_to_notify.value: HMS Nevada Casualty / Gainwell
entity_to_notify.note: User-approved promotion on November 8, 2026 following the eight-state PI/WC parity review. Use the established PI casualty/TPL notification route for WC medical-cost recovery within the same payer/local scope. No affirmative evidence of a separate WC notification recipient, mechanism or exclusion was identified. This is an attributed user-confirmed parity decision, not a claim that every agency expressly states identical PI/WC procedures. NRS 422.293 subrogates the Authority to medical-cost rights against a liable third party. NRS 422.293001 imposes written notice by the recipient asserting a claim or counsel agreeing to representation, using a broad right-to-payment definition. It does not publish separate tort/WC notice procedures. Nevada Medicaid identifies HMS casualty/subrogation separately from insurance-record updates. WC parity follows from that broad notice framework. Notification parity only. Published notice contents, triggers and attachments remain applicable. Disclosure authority, case-opening completion, itemized/interim/final claims, settlement, payment and managed-care/local allocation remain separately scoped. Retain statutory written notice contents. Casualty notification and insurance-record update/escalation are different functions.

entity_to_notify.value: Rhode Island EOHHS / Medicaid Recovery Network (MRN) — attorney matching/lookup; insurer statutory reporting
entity_to_notify.note: November 8 RI role review: Chapter 27-57.1 places database participation and pre-payment checks on insurers, including WC insurers. MRN expressly offers attorneys data matching or interactive recipient lookup. EOHHS provides the intercept notice to the claimant and attorney under section 27-57.1-1(c). The prior first-notice hold incorrectly demanded a separate attorney new-case notification address instead of recognizing this role-specific lookup workflow. Attorney access to the MRN matching/recipient-lookup workflow for covered Rhode Island liability and workers compensation insurance claims. The statutory intercept threshold is payments of $500 or more. This is not a new recovery-file submission, a claim that counsel has no other duties, or a final lien/settlement clearance. Recipient cooperation under 40-6-9(d), MRN exclusions and later lien/appeal/payment issues remain separate.

A separate attorney new-case notification address is not required to establish this published lookup workflow.

# Third Party Liability - Casualty Recovery Casualty recovery's function is to identify and recover money paid on behalf of a Medicaid member for services resulting from any accident or incident for which a third party is liable. ## About Lien Recovery for Settlements

Third-party payments may come from health insurance, settlements or court awards (such as accident, product liability, or malpractice claims), or workers’ compensation.

**Third-Party Liability (TPL)** is the legal requirement for health care carriers to pay all or part of a Medicaid member’s medical claim. Medicaid is the payer of last resort, covering costs only when no other liable payer exists.

In Iowa, Medicaid includes both **Fee-for-Service (FFS)** and the managed care program, **IA Health Link**, which began April 1, 2016. Most members are served through three Managed Care Organizations (MCOs): **Iowa Total Care, Molina, and Wellpoint**. A small percentage remain in FFS.

For FFS members with injuries on or after April 1, 2016, cases must be reported to the **Iowa Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit**. In all other cases, attorneys and carriers should work directly with the member’s MCO.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

## Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

## List items for Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

### Examples

- If an injury happened prior to April 1, 2016, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services incurred before April 1, 2016.

It does not publish separate tort/WC notice procedures. Nevada Medicaid identifies HMS casualty/subrogation separately from insurance-record updates. WC parity follows from that broad notice framework. Use NVCasualty@gainwelltechnologies.com / 888-378-2836 and the existing written route. Include the statutory identifiers, incident date, adverse-party/insurer details if known, and short claim statement. Do not substitute the TPL insurance-record escalation mailbox.

## Third Party Liability (TPL)

The Third Party Liability Unit is responsible for identifying, managing and
recovering funds for claims paid for by Florida Medicaid for which a third party
was liable, thereby ensuring Medicaid is the payer of last resort. TPL recovery
services are contracted with Health Management Systems (HMS), Inc. Some examples
of liable third parties include: Medicare and other insurance companies,
tort/casualty settlements, recipient estates, and trust and annuity recovery.
New or updated third party insurance information is also added to the Florida
Medicaid Management Information System (FMMIS) in order to cost avoid claims
that are submitted by Medicaid providers. When a provider submits a claim and a
recipient has other insurance, the provider is instructed to bill the other
insurance company prior to billing Medicaid. In addition, the TPL Unit also
works in conjunction with the Agency's Bureau of Medicaid Program Integrity to
conduct other Medicaid recoupment projects such as: overpayments, duplicate
payments, provider audits, and overutilization.

Notices to Florida Medicaid regarding any third-party benefit, including trust,
annuity, or estate probate actions, must be submitted in accordance with
sections 409.910, 409.9101, and 733.2121, Florida Statutes (F.S.), to the
appropriate address located below.

Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program

# Florida Medicaid Casualty Recovery Program

Section 1902(a)(25) of the Social Security Act, 42 CFR 433.135, requires that States take all reasonable measures to ascertain the legal liability of third parties to pay for medical services furnished to a Medicaid recipient. Pursuant to 1902(a)(25), Florida Statute Section 409.910 provides that the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) collect all amounts determined available from liable third parties.

**The subsection further requires that recipients or their legal representatives notify the Agency of the existence of any third party benefits.**

Furthermore, the Agency has a statutory lien for the full amount of medical care furnished. This lien attaches and is perfected automatically when a recipient first receives treatment for which the Agency may be obligated to provide payment under the Medicaid program.

Health Management Systems (HMS), a Gainwell Technologies Company, is the authorized agent of the Agency for Health Care Administration (Agency) contracted to identify, manage, and recover all Florida Medicaid paid funds when a Florida Medicaid recipient is involved in a tort or a casualty accident / incident. If you are an attorney with a Florida Medicaid recipient client involved in a tort accident /incident, or if you are an insurance adjuster involved in a case where a Florida Medicaid recipient was injured please do the following:

1\. Complete a [Tort Information Form](https://submissions.hms.com/submissions/tort/tortInfoForm.do) found on this website or send a letter of representation to the Florida TPL Recovery Unit. Along with the Tort Information Form or letter of representation, please include a HIPAA-compliant Medical Release signed by the Medicaid recipient. If you send a letter of representation, please be sure to include at a minimum:

- Recipient Name
- Recipient SSN
- Recipient DOB
- Date of accident or incident
- Details of accident or incident

2\. Submit the Tort Information Form via this website. Send the letter of representation and/or HIPAA-compliant Medical Release form to the following address:

Florida Medicaid Casualty Recovery Program

Attn: HIPAA-Compliant Medical Release

P.O. Box 12188

Tallahassee, FL 32317

When the form /letter and release is received, the data will be entered into our Case Management System. The case will be assigned to a Recovery Specialist. The Recovery Specialist will analyze the case to determine what claims, if any, AHCA paid, related to the accident/incident. Once analyzed, you will receive:

- A Notice of Lien indicating the initial lien amount. (Detailed lien information will be provided only if a HIPAA-compliant Medical Release is on file.); or
- A letter stating the individual could not be identified as a Florida Medicaid recipient, along with a request to verify the information or provide additional information; or
- A letter requesting the missing items – if the request is incomplete

Please note that medical providers have one year from the date of service to bill AHCA. Accordingly, you must request an updated lien amount at the time of settlement.

If you have any questions, please feel free to [contact us](https://www.flmedicaidtplrecovery.com/flmedicaidtplrecovery.com/contact/index.html).

# Authorization for the Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information

**Federal law states that we cannot share an individual’s health information without the individual’s permission, except in certain situations.  By 
signing this form, you are giving us permission to share the information you indicate below.  If you decide later that you do not want us to share 
this information any more, you can revoke this authorization at any time in writing or sign the REVOCATION SECTION on the back of this form 
and return it to the Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program. This form must be completed and signed by the Medicaid recipient or by an 
individual who has the authority to act on the Medicaid recipient’s behalf (parent of a minor, legal guardian, trustee, power of attorney, personal 
representative of the estate, grantor of an annuity).**

### 5. Enter the specific date that you want this authorization to expire: (i.e., one year from date of release)____________________________

(If you do not enter a date, this authorization will expire in five years.)

I understand that the information described above may be redisclosed by the person or group that I hereby give AHCA and its contract representatives

AHCA, its workforce members, and its contract representatives from all liability arising from the disclosure of my health information pursuant to this 
agreement.  I understand that I may inspect or request copies of any information disclosed by this authorization if AHCA or its contract representatives

## INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE USE AND DISCLOSURE OF PROTECTED HEALTH INFORMATION

1. Complete the front of the form and return it to Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program, Post Office Box 12188, Tallahassee, Florida
32317-2188, Phone (toll-free) (877) 357-3268 or Fax (844) 845-8352.

2. If the signer is a guardian, has a power of attorney or is an authorized representative, documentation of the representative’s authority
to act on the individual’s behalf must be attached.  If an agency has custody of a child and a representative signs the release, include a
copy of the custody order.

3. Special kinds of health information have specific laws and rules that have to be followed before that information can be disclosed.

**HIV and Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STD):**  All information about HIV and sexually transmitted diseases is protected under federal 
and state laws and cannot be disclosed without your written authorization unless otherwise provided in the regulations.  To release HIV 
or STD information, this authorization must include a statement in the Information You Want Disclosed section of the specific HIV or STD 
information that you are giving permission to release.  Re-disclosure of HIV information is not allowed, except in compliance with law or 
with your written permission.

**Alcohol and Drug Treatment:**  Alcohol and/or drug treatment records are protected under federal and state laws and regulations and 
cannot be disclosed without your written authorization, unless otherwise provided for in federal and state laws or regulations.  To release 
alcohol and drug treatment information, this authorization must include a statement in the Information You Want Disclosed section of the 
specific information that you are giving permission to release, such as “assessment, treatment plan, attendance, discharge plan.”  Redisclosure of you alcohol and/or drug treatment records is not allowed, except in compliance with law or with your written permission.

**Mental Health Treatment:**  Mental health treatment records are protected under federal and state laws and regulations and cannot be 
disclosed without your written authorization, unless otherwise allowed in federal and state laws or regulations.  To release mental health 
treatment information, this authorization must include a statement in the Information You Want Disclosed section of the specific 
information that you are giving permission to release, such as “assessment, treatment plan, attendance, discharge plan.”  Also, disclosure 
of your therapist’s own notes (psychotherapy notes) needs separate permission.  Re-disclosure of your mental health treatment records 
is prohibited, except in compliance with law or with your written permission.

4. You will be provided with a copy of this form.

## Third Party Liability (TPL)

The Third Party Liability Unit is responsible for identifying, managing and
recovering funds for claims paid for by Florida Medicaid for which a third party
was liable, thereby ensuring Medicaid is the payer of last resort. TPL recovery
services are contracted with Health Management Systems (HMS), Inc. Some examples
of liable third parties include: Medicare and other insurance companies,
tort/casualty settlements, recipient estates, and trust and annuity recovery.
New or updated third party insurance information is also added to the Florida
Medicaid Management Information System (FMMIS) in order to cost avoid claims
that are submitted by Medicaid providers. When a provider submits a claim and a
recipient has other insurance, the provider is instructed to bill the other
insurance company prior to billing Medicaid. In addition, the TPL Unit also
works in conjunction with the Agency's Bureau of Medicaid Program Integrity to
conduct other Medicaid recoupment projects such as: overpayments, duplicate
payments, provider audits, and overutilization.

Notices to Florida Medicaid regarding any third-party benefit, including trust,
annuity, or estate probate actions, must be submitted in accordance with
sections 409.910, 409.9101, and 733.2121, Florida Statutes (F.S.), to the
appropriate address located below.

Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program

# Florida Medicaid Casualty Recovery Program

Section 1902(a)(25) of the Social Security Act, 42 CFR 433.135, requires that States take all reasonable measures to ascertain the legal liability of third parties to pay for medical services furnished to a Medicaid recipient. Pursuant to 1902(a)(25), Florida Statute Section 409.910 provides that the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) collect all amounts determined available from liable third parties.

**The subsection further requires that recipients or their legal representatives notify the Agency of the existence of any third party benefits.**

Furthermore, the Agency has a statutory lien for the full amount of medical care furnished. This lien attaches and is perfected automatically when a recipient first receives treatment for which the Agency may be obligated to provide payment under the Medicaid program.

Health Management Systems (HMS), a Gainwell Technologies Company, is the authorized agent of the Agency for Health Care Administration (Agency) contracted to identify, manage, and recover all Florida Medicaid paid funds when a Florida Medicaid recipient is involved in a tort or a casualty accident / incident. If you are an attorney with a Florida Medicaid recipient client involved in a tort accident /incident, or if you are an insurance adjuster involved in a case where a Florida Medicaid recipient was injured please do the following:

1\. Complete a [Tort Information Form](https://submissions.hms.com/submissions/tort/tortInfoForm.do) found on this website or send a letter of representation to the Florida TPL Recovery Unit. Along with the Tort Information Form or letter of representation, please include a HIPAA-compliant Medical Release signed by the Medicaid recipient. If you send a letter of representation, please be sure to include at a minimum:

- Recipient Name
- Recipient SSN
- Recipient DOB
- Date of accident or incident
- Details of accident or incident

2\. Submit the Tort Information Form via this website. Send the letter of representation and/or HIPAA-compliant Medical Release form to the following address:

Florida Medicaid Casualty Recovery Program

Attn: HIPAA-Compliant Medical Release

P.O. Box 12188

Tallahassee, FL 32317

When the form /letter and release is received, the data will be entered into our Case Management System. The case will be assigned to a Recovery Specialist. The Recovery Specialist will analyze the case to determine what claims, if any, AHCA paid, related to the accident/incident. Once analyzed, you will receive:

- A Notice of Lien indicating the initial lien amount. (Detailed lien information will be provided only if a HIPAA-compliant Medical Release is on file.); or
- A letter stating the individual could not be identified as a Florida Medicaid recipient, along with a request to verify the information or provide additional information; or
- A letter requesting the missing items – if the request is incomplete

Please note that medical providers have one year from the date of service to bill AHCA. Accordingly, you must request an updated lien amount at the time of settlement.

If you have any questions, please feel free to [contact us](https://www.flmedicaidtplrecovery.com/flmedicaidtplrecovery.com/contact/index.html).

# Authorization for the Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information

**Federal law states that we cannot share an individual’s health information without the individual’s permission, except in certain situations.  By 
signing this form, you are giving us permission to share the information you indicate below.  If you decide later that you do not want us to share 
this information any more, you can revoke this authorization at any time in writing or sign the REVOCATION SECTION on the back of this form 
and return it to the Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program. This form must be completed and signed by the Medicaid recipient or by an 
individual who has the authority to act on the Medicaid recipient’s behalf (parent of a minor, legal guardian, trustee, power of attorney, personal 
representative of the estate, grantor of an annuity).**

## INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE USE AND DISCLOSURE OF PROTECTED HEALTH INFORMATION

1. Complete the front of the form and return it to Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program, Post Office Box 12188, Tallahassee, Florida
32317-2188, Phone (toll-free) (877) 357-3268 or Fax (844) 845-8352.

2. If the signer is a guardian, has a power of attorney or is an authorized representative, documentation of the representative’s authority
to act on the individual’s behalf must be attached.  If an agency has custody of a child and a representative signs the release, include a
copy of the custody order.

3. Special kinds of health information have specific laws and rules that have to be followed before that information can be disclosed.

**HIV and Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STD):**  All information about HIV and sexually transmitted diseases is protected under federal 
and state laws and cannot be disclosed without your written authorization unless otherwise provided in the regulations.  To release HIV 
or STD information, this authorization must include a statement in the Information You Want Disclosed section of the specific HIV or STD 
information that you are giving permission to release.  Re-disclosure of HIV information is not allowed, except in compliance with law or 
with your written permission.

**Alcohol and Drug Treatment:**  Alcohol and/or drug treatment records are protected under federal and state laws and regulations and 
cannot be disclosed without your written authorization, unless otherwise provided for in federal and state laws or regulations.  To release 
alcohol and drug treatment information, this authorization must include a statement in the Information You Want Disclosed section of the 
specific information that you are giving permission to release, such as “assessment, treatment plan, attendance, discharge plan.”  Redisclosure of you alcohol and/or drug treatment records is not allowed, except in compliance with law or with your written permission.

**Mental Health Treatment:**  Mental health treatment records are protected under federal and state laws and regulations and cannot be 
disclosed without your written authorization, unless otherwise allowed in federal and state laws or regulations.  To release mental health 
treatment information, this authorization must include a statement in the Information You Want Disclosed section of the specific 
information that you are giving permission to release, such as “assessment, treatment plan, attendance, discharge plan.”  Also, disclosure 
of your therapist’s own notes (psychotherapy notes) needs separate permission.  Re-disclosure of your mental health treatment records 
is prohibited, except in compliance with law or with your written permission.

## Third Party Liability (TPL)

The Third Party Liability Unit is responsible for identifying, managing and
recovering funds for claims paid for by Florida Medicaid for which a third party
was liable, thereby ensuring Medicaid is the payer of last resort. TPL recovery
services are contracted with Health Management Systems (HMS), Inc. Some examples
of liable third parties include: Medicare and other insurance companies,
tort/casualty settlements, recipient estates, and trust and annuity recovery.
New or updated third party insurance information is also added to the Florida
Medicaid Management Information System (FMMIS) in order to cost avoid claims
that are submitted by Medicaid providers. When a provider submits a claim and a
recipient has other insurance, the provider is instructed to bill the other
insurance company prior to billing Medicaid. In addition, the TPL Unit also
works in conjunction with the Agency's Bureau of Medicaid Program Integrity to
conduct other Medicaid recoupment projects such as: overpayments, duplicate
payments, provider audits, and overutilization.

Notices to Florida Medicaid regarding any third-party benefit, including trust,
annuity, or estate probate actions, must be submitted in accordance with
sections 409.910, 409.9101, and 733.2121, Florida Statutes (F.S.), to the
appropriate address located below.

Florida Medicaid TPL Recovery Program

# Florida Medicaid Casualty Recovery Program

Section 1902(a)(25) of the Social Security Act, 42 CFR 433.135, requires that States take all reasonable measures to ascertain the legal liability of third parties to pay for medical services furnished to a Medicaid recipient. Pursuant to 1902(a)(25), Florida Statute Section 409.910 provides that the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) collect all amounts determined available from liable third parties.

**The subsection further requires that recipients or their legal representatives notify the Agency of the existence of any third party benefits.**

Furthermore, the Agency has a statutory lien for the full amount of medical care furnished. This lien attaches and is perfected automatically when a recipient first receives treatment for which the Agency may be obligated to provide payment under the Medicaid program.

Health Management Systems (HMS), a Gainwell Technologies Company, is the authorized agent of the Agency for Health Care Administration (Agency) contracted to identify, manage, and recover all Florida Medicaid paid funds when a Florida Medicaid recipient is involved in a tort or a casualty accident / incident. If you are an attorney with a Florida Medicaid recipient client involved in a tort accident /incident, or if you are an insurance adjuster involved in a case where a Florida Medicaid recipient was injured please do the following:

1\. Complete a [Tort Information Form](https://submissions.hms.com/submissions/tort/tortInfoForm.do) found on this website or send a letter of representation to the Florida TPL Recovery Unit. Along with the Tort Information Form or letter of representation, please include a HIPAA-compliant Medical Release signed by the Medicaid recipient. If you send a letter of representation, please be sure to include at a minimum:

- Recipient Name
- Recipient SSN
- Recipient DOB
- Date of accident or incident
- Details of accident or incident

2\. Submit the Tort Information Form via this website. Send the letter of representation and/or HIPAA-compliant Medical Release form to the following address:

Florida Medicaid Casualty Recovery Program

Attn: HIPAA-Compliant Medical Release

P.O. Box 12188

Tallahassee, FL 32317

When the form /letter and release is received, the data will be entered into our Case Management System. The case will be assigned to a Recovery Specialist. The Recovery Specialist will analyze the case to determine what claims, if any, AHCA paid, related to the accident/incident. Once analyzed, you will receive:

- A Notice of Lien indicating the initial lien amount. (Detailed lien information will be provided only if a HIPAA-compliant Medical Release is on file.); or
- A letter stating the individual could not be identified as a Florida Medicaid recipient, along with a request to verify the information or provide additional information; or
- A letter requesting the missing items – if the request is incomplete

Please note that medical providers have one year from the date of service to bill AHCA. Accordingly, you must request an updated lien amount at the time of settlement.

If you have any questions, please feel free to [contact us](https://www.flmedicaidtplrecovery.com/flmedicaidtplrecovery.com/contact/index.html).

Georgia Medicaid’s Subrogation, Estate Recovery and Special Needs Trust programs are administered by Health Management System (HMS). The Department of Community Health (DCH) oversees the administration of Georgia’s Medicaid and PeachCare for Kids® programs. HMS contracts with DCH to operate the Subrogation Unit, Estate Recovery Unit and Trust Unit.

## Subrogation Unit

The Subrogation Unit is responsible for enforcing DCH’s rights to recovery in subrogation claims, and for ensuring that the State receives its reimbursement. The Subrogation Unit’s purpose is to recover the cost of medical expenditures from liable third parties when members are involved in a personal injury action. These suits may be related to an auto accident, medical malpractice claim, general liability, worker’s compensation, mass torts, or any other tort claim where a settlement has been reached or a judgment has been awarded.

To notify DCH of an action, please print and complete the transmittal form and fax it or your standard letter of representation to our office at 855-467-3970 or by email at [gacasualty@gainwelltechnologies.com](mailto:gacasualty@gainwelltechnologies.com). The Subrogation Unit will contact you with the subrogation amount to help you settle your claim. If you require a breakdown of the bills paid by DCH, please include a signed medical authorization. A link to the medical authorization form can be found under the forms menu.

Please note that the Department of Community Health has three rights to recovery:

- Subrogation (Claims against liable third parties)
- Assignment (Medicaid Members assign their rights to tort settlements to DCH as a condition of eligibility)
- Department Lien (State and federal law allows DCH to place a lien in the amount of Medicaid expenditures for injuries to Members for which third parties are liable)

# Authorization to Release Member Information Form

## LEGAL BASIS

Based on the Privacy Rule of the Health Inf ormation Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), TennCare must receive authorization and consent to release your information in most cases when the purpose of the disclosure is not directly related to TennCare’s Treatment, Payment or Healthcare Operations activities (45 CFR 164.508). TennCare includes programs like TennCare Medicaid, CHOICES, and CoverKids.

## INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION

- **Complete and Submit the Form to TennCare and Member’s Managed Care Organization (MCO)** You must complete pages 2 and 3 of the subrogation request form and submit them directly to TennCare and member’s MCO. Submission instructions f or subrogation requests are available on the TennCare website under the <u>Subrogation</u>.
- **Need Help Submitting the Form Securely?** If you have concerns about sending private information and would like assistance with a secure submission method, you may contact the TennCare Privacy Of f ice at <u>Privacy.TennCare@tn.gov</u>.
## IMPORTANT INFORMATION

- Giving your permission is up to you. You don’t have to share your health facts.
- You don’t have to sign this form if you don’t want to, and you don’t need to send your information to anyone you don’t want to. You will still get benefits and treatment.
- You can take back your permission. You must tell us in writing. Mail it or email it using the contact information above.
- What if you take back your permission? It won’t take back the health facts we have already shared. But, we won’t share any more of your health facts.
- If we share your health facts with the people or agencies you named, they may share it with others. Not everyone has to follow privacy rules.
**You have a right to get a copy of the permission you gave us**. If you need another copy, call the TennCare Privacy Office at **1-866-797-9469.** We can charge for copies of records as allowed by law.

## OTHER IMPORTANT INFORMATION

You always have the right to file a privacy complaint **Division of TennCare U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services Region** Attn: Privacy Office **IV, Office of Civil Rights** 310 Great Circle Road Nashville, TN 37243 Medical Privacy, Complaint Division Phone: 1-866-797-9469 Atlanta Federal Center Suite 3B70 61 Forsyth Street, Email: Privacy.TennCare@tn.gov SW Atlanta, GA 30303-0064 Customer Response Center: (800) 368-1019 Fax: (202) 619-3818 TDD: (800) 537-7697 Email: <u>ocrmail@hhs.gov</u> You will **not be punished** if you ask f or help or if you make a complaint.

Puede obtener estas hojas en español. Visite nuestro sitio web en tn.gov/tenncare. O bien, llame **TennCare Connect** al **855-259-0701.**

### 1. Who is the Member?

Name of Member (Last, First, Middle Initial): ____________________________________________________________ Phone Number: ___________________________ ID Number (Member ID or last 4 digits of SSN): __________________________________ Date of Birth (MM/DD/YYYY): __________________________________ Address: ________________________________________________________________________________________ City: ______________________________________ State: _______________________ and Zip Code: ____________ Email: __________________________________________ Who is completing this form? Check One: I am the Member OR I have the legal right to act for this person. (Check one below; if “other” fill in blank.) Legal Guardian Authorized Representative Other (please describe):______________________________

### 2. Who can my health facts be given to?

Name (like family members who live with me, or a place of business): **_________________________________________** Organization Name (if you want to send to an organization): **_________________________________________________** Address: **___________________________________________________________________________________________** City: ____________________________________ State: _______________________ and Zip Code: **_________________** Phone Number (with area code): **___________________________________**

### 3. What health facts can we share?

We’ll only share the health facts and records you allow and we have. Tell us the health facts and records you allow us to share. Give the date or place they come from if you can. Health Fact(s): ___________________________________________________________________________________ Date(s) I Received Care (if applicable): _______________________________ Name of the Place(s) I Received Care (if applicable): _____________________________________________________ If you give us your OK to share these other kinds of health information, tell us by checking the boxes. HIV/AIDS Alcohol/Substance Abuse Records Sexual/Physical/Mental Abuse Records Mental Health Records For any health facts you gave your **OK** share, facts we share may include medicine you take now or have taken. It doesn’t include psycho-therapy notes, which you must OK separate from any other facts.

### 4. Why are you giving out this health information?

Is it to get health treatment, for court or work? Or are you asking for these records to be sent directly to you f or your own use? Please describe: ___________________________________________________________________________________

Puede obtener estas hojas en español. Visite nuestro sitio web en www.tennessee.gov/tenncare. O bien, llame **TennCare** **Connect** al **855-259-0701**.

### 5. When does my permission end?

We have your permission for as long as you tell us we do, but this permission can’t be for more than 1 year. Tell us when to stop sharing your health facts**. If you don’t tell us how long your permission lasts, then we will end your permission** **one year from when you sign.** My OK ends on this date: _____________________________ OR My OK ends when this happens: _____________________________________________________________________ (It can be something like “you can share my medical records this one time.”)

### 6. Signature of the Member (if Member is signing)

I give my **OK** to share the information listed in this form. This form can be an original or a copy. Signature or Mark (“X”) of Member: ______________________________________ Date: _________________________ If signed “X” please tell us the person’s name who helped you: _______________________________________________ Helper’s phone number: _________________________ Helper’s Address: ___________________________________________________________________________________ City: _______________________________________ State: ________________ Zip Code: _________________________

### 7. Signature of the Authorized Representative (if somebody else is signing)

**Authorized Representative** means you have legal proof you can act for this person. You must give us a copy of this proof. A representative must sign for a member who cannot legally sign on his or her own. If the patient is less than 18 years old, a parent or guardian should sign for the minor. Signature of Person signing on behalf of patient: ____________________________________ D at e: _________________ Printed Name: _________________________________________________ Phone: ______________________________ Address: ___________________________________________________________________________________________ City: _______________________________________ State: ________________ Zip Code: _________________________

## NOTICE TO ANY RECIPIENT OTHER THAN THE MEMBER

This information has been disclosed to you from records the confidentiality of which may be protected by federal and/or state law. If the records are protected under the federal regulations on the confidentiality of alcohol and drug abuse patient records (42 CFR Part 2), you are prohibited from making any further disclosure of this information unless further disclosure is expressly permitted by the written consent of the person to whom it pertains, or as otherwise permitted by 42 CFR Part 2. A general authorization for the release of medical or other information is NOT sufficient for this purpose. The federal rules restrict use of the information to criminally investigate or prosecute any alcohol or drug abuse patient.

# Authorization to Release Member Information Form

## LEGAL BASIS

Based on the Privacy Rule of the Health Inf ormation Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), TennCare must receive authorization and consent to release your information in most cases when the purpose of the disclosure is not directly related to TennCare’s Treatment, Payment or Healthcare Operations activities (45 CFR 164.508). TennCare includes programs like TennCare Medicaid, CHOICES, and CoverKids.

## INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION

- **Complete and Submit the Form to TennCare and Member’s Managed Care Organization (MCO)** You must complete pages 2 and 3 of the subrogation request form and submit them directly to TennCare and member’s MCO. Submission instructions f or subrogation requests are available on the TennCare website under the <u>Subrogation</u>.
- **Need Help Submitting the Form Securely?** If you have concerns about sending private information and would like assistance with a secure submission method, you may contact the TennCare Privacy Of f ice at <u>Privacy.TennCare@tn.gov</u>.
## IMPORTANT INFORMATION

- Giving your permission is up to you. You don’t have to share your health facts.
- You don’t have to sign this form if you don’t want to, and you don’t need to send your information to anyone you don’t want to. You will still get benefits and treatment.
- You can take back your permission. You must tell us in writing. Mail it or email it using the contact information above.
- What if you take back your permission? It won’t take back the health facts we have already shared. But, we won’t share any more of your health facts.
- If we share your health facts with the people or agencies you named, they may share it with others. Not everyone has to follow privacy rules.
**You have a right to get a copy of the permission you gave us**. If you need another copy, call the TennCare Privacy Office at **1-866-797-9469.** We can charge for copies of records as allowed by law.

## OTHER IMPORTANT INFORMATION

You always have the right to file a privacy complaint **Division of TennCare U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services Region** Attn: Privacy Office **IV, Office of Civil Rights** 310 Great Circle Road Nashville, TN 37243 Medical Privacy, Complaint Division Phone: 1-866-797-9469 Atlanta Federal Center Suite 3B70 61 Forsyth Street, Email: Privacy.TennCare@tn.gov SW Atlanta, GA 30303-0064 Customer Response Center: (800) 368-1019 Fax: (202) 619-3818 TDD: (800) 537-7697 Email: <u>ocrmail@hhs.gov</u> You will **not be punished** if you ask f or help or if you make a complaint.

### 5. When does my permission end?

We have your permission for as long as you tell us we do, but this permission can’t be for more than 1 year. Tell us when to stop sharing your health facts**. **Authorized Representative** means you have legal proof you can act for this person. You must give us a copy of this proof. ## NOTICE TO ANY RECIPIENT OTHER THAN THE MEMBER

This information has been disclosed to you from records the confidentiality of which may be protected by federal and/or state law. If the records are protected under the federal regulations on the confidentiality of alcohol and drug abuse patient records (42 CFR Part 2), you are prohibited from making any further disclosure of this information unless further disclosure is expressly permitted by the written consent of the person to whom it pertains, or as otherwise permitted by 42 CFR Part 2. A general authorization for the release of medical or other information is NOT sufficient for this purpose. The federal rules restrict use of the information to criminally investigate or prosecute any alcohol or drug abuse patient.

## Information to include in notification of injury or claim

If you are an Apple Health client, you may have received a treatment questionnaire following your accident or injury. It is important you fill out the form and return it to HCA. HCA Casualty Unit will contact the insurance company listed on the form and/or your attorney if you have one.

If you represent an Apple Health client, provide notification of a new case by submitting a request in our [support portal](https://support.hca.wa.gov/hcasupport). We will need a [HIPAA compliant medical authorization](https://www.hca.wa.gov/assets/free-or-low-cost/80-020-release-information-authorization.pdf) naming the Health Care Authority to provide you with a claims ledger.

Don't get delayed

Include **only one client** per correspondence. We cannot process multiple clients in the same communication.

[What happens when an Apple Health member's claim or lawsuit has resolved?](https://www.hca.wa.gov/about-hca/other-administrative-activities/personal-injury-casualty-recoveries-and-special-needs-trusts#WhathappenswhenanAppleHealthmembersclaimorlawsuithasresolved)

To expedite your request, include the following information regarding the injured client, in your letter of representation. This information helps us determine if we have a subrogated interest.

- Full name
- Social security number or ProviderOne number (9-digit number end with WA)
- Date and type of accident
- Type of injury(ies) sustained and whether treatment has concluded (provide date of last treatment)
- Name of attorney handling the case
- Contact information for insurance company and claims adjustor, including the following:
  - Claim number
  - Policy number
  - Whether PIP/MedPay is available

[What if the attorney changes?](https://www.hca.wa.gov/about-hca/other-administrative-activities/personal-injury-casualty-recoveries-and-special-needs-trusts#Whatiftheattorneychanges)

Send your notification to one of the following:

- **Email (preferred):** [HCA Casualty Unit](mailto:HCACasualtyUnit@hca.wa.gov)(PDF documents preferred)

  - **Fax:** 360-753-3077
  - **Mail to:**


     The Health Care Authority


     PO Box 45561


     Olympia, WA 98504-5561

[What happens when an Apple Health member's claim or lawsuit has resolved?](https://www.hca.wa.gov/about-hca/other-administrative-activities/personal-injury-casualty-recoveries-and-special-needs-trusts#WhathappenswhenanAppleHealthmembersclaimorlawsuithasresolved)

Contact us once a claim or lawsuit has been resolved, and before any settlement funds are released to the Apple Health client. We will need the following documentation to calculate HCA's proportionate share of fees and costs under RCW 41.05A.070(4)(c):

- Signed copy of the settlement or release;
- Signed copy of attorney's fee agreement with the client or, if fees were not charged according to the agreement, confirmation of the actual fee charged; and
- An itemized statement of attorney costs.

We request these documents in all cases so we can determine the final amount due to HCA.

Once we receive the information, we will calculate the final amount to pay and send payment instructions.

[What if the attorney changes?](https://www.hca.wa.gov/about-hca/other-administrative-activities/personal-injury-casualty-recoveries-and-special-needs-trusts#Whatiftheattorneychanges)

Notify us if the Apple Health client's legal representative changes.

# Authorization to Release Member Information Form

## LEGAL BASIS

Based on the Privacy Rule of the Health Inf ormation Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), TennCare must receive authorization and consent to release your information in most cases when the purpose of the disclosure is not directly related to TennCare’s Treatment, Payment or Healthcare Operations activities (45 CFR 164.508). TennCare includes programs like TennCare Medicaid, CHOICES, and CoverKids.

## INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION

- **Complete and Submit the Form to TennCare and Member’s Managed Care Organization (MCO)** You must complete pages 2 and 3 of the subrogation request form and submit them directly to TennCare and member’s MCO. Submission instructions f or subrogation requests are available on the TennCare website under the <u>Subrogation</u>.
- **Need Help Submitting the Form Securely?** If you have concerns about sending private information and would like assistance with a secure submission method, you may contact the TennCare Privacy Of f ice at <u>Privacy.TennCare@tn.gov</u>.
## IMPORTANT INFORMATION

- Giving your permission is up to you. You don’t have to share your health facts.
- You don’t have to sign this form if you don’t want to, and you don’t need to send your information to anyone you don’t want to. You will still get benefits and treatment.
- You can take back your permission. You must tell us in writing. Mail it or email it using the contact information above.
- What if you take back your permission? It won’t take back the health facts we have already shared. But, we won’t share any more of your health facts.
- If we share your health facts with the people or agencies you named, they may share it with others. Not everyone has to follow privacy rules.
**You have a right to get a copy of the permission you gave us**. If you need another copy, call the TennCare Privacy Office at **1-866-797-9469.** We can charge for copies of records as allowed by law.

## OTHER IMPORTANT INFORMATION

You always have the right to file a privacy complaint **Division of TennCare U.S. Dept. of Health and Human Services Region** Attn: Privacy Office **IV, Office of Civil Rights** 310 Great Circle Road Nashville, TN 37243 Medical Privacy, Complaint Division Phone: 1-866-797-9469 Atlanta Federal Center Suite 3B70 61 Forsyth Street, Email: Privacy.TennCare@tn.gov SW Atlanta, GA 30303-0064 Customer Response Center: (800) 368-1019 Fax: (202) 619-3818 TDD: (800) 537-7697 Email: <u>ocrmail@hhs.gov</u> You will **not be punished** if you ask f or help or if you make a complaint.

Check One: I am the Member OR I have the legal right to act for this person. (Check one below; if “other” fill in blank.) Legal Guardian Authorized Representative Other (please describe):______________________________

### 2. Who can my health facts be given to?

Name (like family members who live with me, or a place of business): **_________________________________________** Organization Name (if you want to send to an organization): **_________________________________________________** Address: **___________________________________________________________________________________________** City: ____________________________________ State: _______________________ and Zip Code: **_________________** Phone Number (with area code): **___________________________________**

### 3. What health facts can we share?

We’ll only share the health facts and records you allow and we have. Tell us the health facts and records you allow us to share. Give the date or place they come from if you can. Health Fact(s): ___________________________________________________________________________________ Date(s) I Received Care (if applicable): _______________________________ Name of the Place(s) I Received Care (if applicable): _____________________________________________________ If you give us your OK to share these other kinds of health information, tell us by checking the boxes. HIV/AIDS Alcohol/Substance Abuse Records Sexual/Physical/Mental Abuse Records Mental Health Records For any health facts you gave your **OK** share, facts we share may include medicine you take now or have taken. It doesn’t include psycho-therapy notes, which you must OK separate from any other facts.

### 4. Why are you giving out this health information?

Is it to get health treatment, for court or work? Or are you asking for these records to be sent directly to you f or your own use? Please describe: ___________________________________________________________________________________

### 5. When does my permission end?

We have your permission for as long as you tell us we do, but this permission can’t be for more than 1 year. Tell us when to stop sharing your health facts**. If you don’t tell us how long your permission lasts, then we will end your permission** **one year from when you sign.** My OK ends on this date: _____________________________ OR My OK ends when this happens: _____________________________________________________________________ (It can be something like “you can share my medical records this one time.”)

I give my **OK** to share the information listed in this form. This form can be an original or a copy. ### 7. Signature of the Authorized Representative (if somebody else is signing)

**Authorized Representative** means you have legal proof you can act for this person. You must give us a copy of this proof. A representative must sign for a member who cannot legally sign on his or her own. If the patient is less than 18 years old, a parent or guardian should sign for the minor. Signature of Person signing on behalf of patient: ____________________________________ D at e: _________________ Printed Name: _________________________________________________ Phone: ______________________________ Address: ___________________________________________________________________________________________ City: _______________________________________ State: ________________ Zip Code: _________________________

## NOTICE TO ANY RECIPIENT OTHER THAN THE MEMBER

This information has been disclosed to you from records the confidentiality of which may be protected by federal and/or state law. If the records are protected under the federal regulations on the confidentiality of alcohol and drug abuse patient records (42 CFR Part 2), you are prohibited from making any further disclosure of this information unless further disclosure is expressly permitted by the written consent of the person to whom it pertains, or as otherwise permitted by 42 CFR Part 2. A general authorization for the release of medical or other information is NOT sufficient for this purpose. The federal rules restrict use of the information to criminally investigate or prosecute any alcohol or drug abuse patient.

evidence.passage: # Third Party Liability

## The Third Party Liability Unit (TPL) is responsible for ensuring that the Medicaid program is the payer of last resort. As Medicaid costs go up, it's important to hold third party payers, such as private carriers, Medicare, and the Veterans Administration, responsible before Medicaid provides assistance.

- **Accident and Trauma:** TPL conducts reviews of accident and trauma when Medicaid recipients are injured in a car or work place accident, or other incident such as a fall, that their liability insurance covers. TPL staff review diagnosis and procedure codes on billing claims to determine an accident related injury. Staff also use provider referrals, and inquiries from attorneys and recipients to assist in determination. TPL is authorized to seek reimbursement of funds from injury settlements. If a recipient requests information to be released to a third party, such as a lawyer, a [HIPAA Access to Request Records Request.pdf![PDF document](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt476/files/styles/inline_icon/public/2019-12/icon-pdf.png?h=e77b622d&itok=QwOzQFit)archive![Non-Compliant ADA Archive Document](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/modules/custom/st_ada_archive/assets/icon-ada-archive.svg)](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt476/files/documents/2021-12/hipaa-access-to-records.pdf) must be completed and notarized.

# Third Party Liability - Casualty Recovery

Casualty recovery's function is to identify and recover money paid on behalf of a Medicaid member for services resulting from any accident or incident for which a third party is liable.

These situations include vehicular accidents, injuries caused by defective products (product liability), job-related injuries and medical malpractice. All of these are referred to as casualty or tort cases.

The South Carolina Department of Health and Human Services (SCDHHS) must recover money from out-of-court settlements or court awards that include compensation for medical expenses, since a third party is liable for the medical care provided to beneficiaries due to the cause of action.

Both Fee-for-Service Medicaid and Managed Care Plans are required to pursue casualty recoveries, just as they are required to pursue other types of third-party liability (TPL).

Attorneys should contact the member's plan directly for information about a casualty case.

## About Lien Recovery for Settlements

Third-party payments may come from health insurance, settlements or court awards (such as accident, product liability, or malpractice claims), or workers’ compensation.

**Third-Party Liability (TPL)** is the legal requirement for health care carriers to pay all or part of a Medicaid member’s medical claim. Medicaid is the payer of last resort, covering costs only when no other liable payer exists.

In Iowa, Medicaid includes both **Fee-for-Service (FFS)** and the managed care program, **IA Health Link**, which began April 1, 2016. Most members are served through three Managed Care Organizations (MCOs): **Iowa Total Care, Molina, and Wellpoint**. A small percentage remain in FFS.

For FFS members with injuries on or after April 1, 2016, cases must be reported to the **Iowa Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit**. In all other cases, attorneys and carriers should work directly with the member’s MCO.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

## Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

## List items for Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

### Examples

- If an injury happened prior to April 1, 2016, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services incurred before April 1, 2016.
- If an injury results in claims that include services incurred prior to and after April 1, 2016, the Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for any health service payments related to the injury and incurred prior to April 1, 2016. A service related to the injury on or after April 1, 2016, will be handled by the member’s MCO. The MCO will file a separate lien for services incurred on or after April 1, 2016.
- For injuries that occur on or after April 1, 2016; if the member has the Medicaid FFS, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services prior to their MCO assignment. If the member moves their eligibility to an MCO then the member’s MCO will handle liens for any services incurred after assignment. In instances such as this, the attorney’s office or carrier will need to work with both the IME Revenue Collections Unit and member’s MCO.

Medicaid will request more information from a member when a provider submits a claim for payment that shows the Medicaid member may have been involved in an accident or injury.  Medicaid members who do not return the requested information may lose their Medicaid coverage. Once Medicaid coverage is lost any months that are lost due to non-cooperation are not eligible for Medicaid coverage. To regain Medicaid eligibility, you may need to reapply for Medicaid.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

## About Lien Recovery for Settlements

Third-party payments may come from health insurance, settlements or court awards (such as accident, product liability, or malpractice claims), or workers’ compensation.

**Third-Party Liability (TPL)** is the legal requirement for health care carriers to pay all or part of a Medicaid member’s medical claim. Medicaid is the payer of last resort, covering costs only when no other liable payer exists.

In Iowa, Medicaid includes both **Fee-for-Service (FFS)** and the managed care program, **IA Health Link**, which began April 1, 2016. Most members are served through three Managed Care Organizations (MCOs): **Iowa Total Care, Molina, and Wellpoint**. A small percentage remain in FFS.

For FFS members with injuries on or after April 1, 2016, cases must be reported to the **Iowa Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit**. In all other cases, attorneys and carriers should work directly with the member’s MCO.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

## Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

## List items for Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

### Examples

- If an injury happened prior to April 1, 2016, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services incurred before April 1, 2016.
- If an injury results in claims that include services incurred prior to and after April 1, 2016, the Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for any health service payments related to the injury and incurred prior to April 1, 2016. A service related to the injury on or after April 1, 2016, will be handled by the member’s MCO. The MCO will file a separate lien for services incurred on or after April 1, 2016.
- For injuries that occur on or after April 1, 2016; if the member has the Medicaid FFS, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services prior to their MCO assignment. If the member moves their eligibility to an MCO then the member’s MCO will handle liens for any services incurred after assignment. In instances such as this, the attorney’s office or carrier will need to work with both the IME Revenue Collections Unit and member’s MCO.

Medicaid will request more information from a member when a provider submits a claim for payment that shows the Medicaid member may have been involved in an accident or injury.  Medicaid members who do not return the requested information may lose their Medicaid coverage. Once Medicaid coverage is lost any months that are lost due to non-cooperation are not eligible for Medicaid coverage. To regain Medicaid eligibility, you may need to reapply for Medicaid.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

In Iowa, Medicaid includes both **Fee-for-Service (FFS)** and the managed care program, **IA Health Link**, which began April 1, 2016. Most members are served through three Managed Care Organizations (MCOs): **Iowa Total Care, Molina, and Wellpoint**. A small percentage remain in FFS.

For FFS members with injuries on or after April 1, 2016, cases must be reported to the **Iowa Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit**. In all other cases, attorneys and carriers should work directly with the member’s MCO.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

## Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

## List items for Impact for injuries and Lien Recovery

### Examples

- If an injury happened prior to April 1, 2016, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services incurred before April 1, 2016.
- If an injury results in claims that include services incurred prior to and after April 1, 2016, the Medicaid Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for any health service payments related to the injury and incurred prior to April 1, 2016. A service related to the injury on or after April 1, 2016, will be handled by the member’s MCO. The MCO will file a separate lien for services incurred on or after April 1, 2016.
- For injuries that occur on or after April 1, 2016; if the member has the Medicaid FFS, the IME Revenue Collections Unit will file a lien for services prior to their MCO assignment. If the member moves their eligibility to an MCO then the member’s MCO will handle liens for any services incurred after assignment. In instances such as this, the attorney’s office or carrier will need to work with both the IME Revenue Collections Unit and member’s MCO.

Medicaid will request more information from a member when a provider submits a claim for payment that shows the Medicaid member may have been involved in an accident or injury.  Medicaid members who do not return the requested information may lose their Medicaid coverage. Once Medicaid coverage is lost any months that are lost due to non-cooperation are not eligible for Medicaid coverage. To regain Medicaid eligibility, you may need to reapply for Medicaid.

[Back to top](https://hhs.iowa.gov/medicaid/member-services/member-rights-and-responsibilities/lien-recovery#block-onthispage)

answers.title: Recovery responsibility and plan interests
answers.text: ACOM 434 reserves motor-vehicle, other casualty, tortfeasor, restitution and WC recovery to AHCCCS/its authorized representative unless the matter is referred to the health-plan contractor. AHCCCS’s TPL contractor classifies mass-tort, total-plan and joint cases and refers total-plan cases to the plan. Follow that assignment rather than treating a central contact or plan figure as universal clearance.
answers.scope: Applies to the contractor populations named in ACOM 434. A particular file still follows its actual referral/assignment.

answers.title: Published settlement steps and checklist limits
answers.text: A.R.S. 36-2915(G) provides that an AHCCCS lien may not be amended after final settlement if the administration received notice of the impending settlement at least 15 working days beforehand. Subsections H–I address compromise factors. These provisions do not publish a complete settlement/compromise attachment checklist.
answers.scope: Statutory lien-amendment rule, not a guarantee of final-letter turnaround or waiver of every other lien.

answers.title: Recovery responsibility and plan interests
answers.text: For the Medi-Cal managed-care contract scope, DHCS has exclusive responsibility for casualty, tort and workers’ compensation recovery. The 2024 boilerplate prohibits the plan from making a recovery claim for covered services in those actions and requires claims/utilization information from its provider and subcontractor chain. Verify all relevant payer periods, injury-related services and the final case calculation; exclusive recovery authority does not prove a particular ledger is complete.

answers.title: Reporting the injury
answers.text: Email inquiries and new referrals to the county-specific HFS inbox. The HFS Information Portal also accepts documents and information requests. Plan-paid claims: Refer pertinent case information for suspected or known third-party injury liability to Katch IQ at submitreferrals@katchiq.com. Use the current Medicaid manual’s email, not the superseded 2025 Optum address. General plan inquiry routes: Use ABHILProviderRelations@aetna.com or 866-329-4701 to request plan-side assistance and the assigned casualty handler when no vendor file is known. The April 2026 notice supplies provider TPL assistance, not an express attorney casualty filing instruction. Optum is documented handling an Aetna Illinois lien in the cited court case;  its POBox 182643ColumbusOH 43218 is that record’s lien-payment address. Call 877-860-2837 for BCCHP plan/TPL inquiry and request routing for an injury-recovery matter. The published article concerns provider other-insurance validation and claim disputes;  it does not establish this as a dedicated casualty unit or confirm the parent 800-582-6418 line for Medicaid. Contact countycareproviderservices@cookcountyhhs.org or 312-864-8200,option 3, and request the CountyCare TPL/Finance recovery handler. The October 2026 guide confirms shared provider inquiry contacts;  attorney casualty service and a dedicated subrogation endpoint remain to be established. Do not equate CountyCare plan recovery with a CCH hospital lien. Call Meridian Medicaid 866-606-3700 to identify the assigned subrogation handler;  its official page directs legal matters to Attn:Legal,CentenePlaza,7700ForsythBoulevard,StLouisMO 63105. Rawlings and First Recovery Group are named in the Medicaid payment-code crosswalk;  the court record documents Meridian Medicaid liens with Equian/Rawlings. Confirm the current file’s handler rather than assigning all cases to one vendor. Use ILYouthCare@centene.com or 844-289-2264 for program-specific inquiry and request its casualty-recovery handler. Keep YouthCare identity separate from standard Meridian;  provider claim payerID instructions do not establish attorney notice requirements. DCFS.HealthPlan@illinois.gov/800-232-3798 is coverage/advocacy coordination, not a verified subrogation desk.

answers.title: Reporting the injury
answers.text: Use the LDH TPL Recovery Portal, Trauma Recovery Login, for PI and WC recovery requests, or the published trauma email/fax alternatives. Statutory petition service and MCO notice remain separate. Plan-paid claims: Send subrogation documentation/inquiries to subrogation@amerihealthcaritas.com. The manual directs provider overpayment worksheets or related documentation here; formal attorney first-notice/service requirements remain to be established with this department. Call 855-242-0802 right away for a WC claim, pending PI/medical-malpractice lawsuit or auto accident. The 2026 handbook expressly directs these matters to Member Services; obtain the recovery handler and any attorney-documentation instructions during follow-through. Report pending PI/medical-malpractice lawsuits or auto-accident claims immediately to LHCC; its Other Insurance section provides Member Services 866-595-8133. Ask for the assigned casualty-recovery handler. The old policy’s Rawlings assignment is retained as historical research, not a current direct intake designation. Call Member Services 844-521-6941 right away for a WC claim, pending PI/medical-malpractice lawsuit or auto accident. The August 2026 handbook explicitly directs these matters here; this is the member injury-reporting number, distinct from the provider line. Notify Humana right away for a WC claim, personal injury, medical-malpractice lawsuit or car accident using Member Services 800-448-3810. The 2026 Louisiana Medicaid handbook supplies this plan reporting route; obtain the assigned recovery handler during follow-through. Known legacy plan inquiry route: call 866-675-1607 and ask a run-out advocate for the department responsible for prior UHC-paid casualty/subrogation interests. The published call-center period runs throughSeptember 30,2027. This is historical paid-claims support, not a current Louisiana enrollment plan or proof that a new MCO clears UHC’s earlier interest. General inquiry contact is known and usable. Targeted research concerns the designated casualty recipient or legacy paid-claim holder, not absence of a contact route. User confirms Optum as the operational UHC subrogation route. Use https://subroreferrals.com/ for referral or case-information requests, or call Optum subrogation888-870-8842. The current Katch-branded FAQ describes One Healthcare ID and case setup. Uploads accept PDF,DOC,DOCX or TIFF,with up to3files and a1.95MB maximum per file; provide the pertinent member and accident information. Identify UHC Louisiana,the member and relevant paid-claim/service periods; obtain acceptance or appropriate reassignment within the actual file. UHC run-out866-675-1607 remains backup departmental escalation through the publishedSeptember30,2027period. This known route closes contact research; individual legacy-file acceptance,lien figures and settlement instructions are case follow-through.

answers.title: Recovery responsibility and plan interests
answers.text: An MCO identifies and collects third-party amounts for medical care it furnishes. If both the Department and MCO have subrogation rights, they coordinate settlement negotiations and prorate available funds between their claims. COMAR also permits assignment of the Department’s rights to an MCO with notice to the recipient/attorney. The state and plan interests therefore need to be identified; a state figure alone is not a blanket plan clearance.
answers.scope: Recovery allocation and assignment. The receiving contact in a particular notice controls its own assigned claim.

answers.title: Reporting the injury
answers.text: Notify PI and WC accidents by mail or email to MO HealthNet Cost Recovery; fax is also published. Include a HIPAA release so the unit can speak with counsel. Plan-paid claims: Call 855-694-4663 to report an injury/WC matter. The plan’s subrogation section explicitly supplies this phone; it is also Member Services. Request transfer to the recovery handler and record the case reference. Call 877-236-1020 for WC, pending PI/tort/product-liability/medical-malpractice or auto matters. The 2026 subrogation section explicitly gives this specialty-program number; do not substitute Home State Health’s other-plan number. Call 866-292-0359 to report an injury/accident matter, including work injury, legal representation or accident recovery. The MO HealthNet handbook specifically gives the number in injury and subrogation instructions; request the assigned recovery handler. Report work/car accidents and pending PI/tort/product-liability/medical-malpractice matters to Healthy Blue at 833-388-1407 and notify FSD as the Medicaid handbook instructs. The separate 800-877-6876 accident-questionnaire line is an existing-questionnaire contact, not this initial reporting route.

answers.title: Published settlement steps and checklist limits
answers.text: For settlements subject to §9-5-11, send settlement notice including the amount allocated to Medicaid-paid past medical expenses and retain the asserted lien in escrow. The statute provides a consent/rejection process; where the total settlement is below the lien, consent is required before finalization. Section (d)(4) exempts a fully resolving settlement collectively no greater than $20,000 from this section. The source does not prescribe the office’s complete fee/cost, release or distribution attachment checklist.
answers.scope: Qualified statutory steps, including the stated exemption. No extension of the statute’s past-medical language or computation of a case’s lien.

answers.title: Published lien-supplement requirement
answers.text: Section 9-5-11(c)(4) requires related supplements in a timely manner, no later than 15 days after receipt of a request. Its first-amount notice wording refers to the recipient and third party where the recipient is unrepresented; it does not establish automatic delivery to represented counsel or define a distinct final-demand document.
