personal_injury.what_happens_next.value: After the form/representation letter and signed release, a Recovery Specialist reviews related claims and sends an initial lien or a deficiency/unidentified-member response. The published FAQ expects the initial lien within 21 days; itemization requires a completed release on file. Request an updated amount at settlement.
personal_injury.what_happens_next.note: Florida state-paid PI scope. Published expectation, not an observed guarantee or a notice deadline; separate plan interests remain distinct.

personal_injury.what_happens_next.value: After the signed referral/release package, HMS enters the file and sends a recovery letter, then a related claims printout approximately two to three weeks later. The printout may be interim or final.
personal_injury.what_happens_next.note: Ohio published sequence and approximate response only; do not copy NJ immediate-ID reliability or 60/30/45-day statements.

personal_injury.what_happens_next.value: After the information form and signed release, HMS enters the file and sends a Subrogation/Recovery letter. The recovery page estimates about 10 business days for a claims response; the FAQ says typically two to three weeks. Interim or final statements and related claims are described.
personal_injury.what_happens_next.note: Preserve both published estimates. They are not guarantees or NJ processing times. County/HMO/MCO interests remain separate.

personal_injury.what_happens_next.value: Reporting triggers the initial lien. The HMS case ID arrives in initial correspondence by letter or fax. The reviewer reports no stated initial-lien timeframe.
personal_injury.what_happens_next.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. No NJ processing time or guaranteed response period is imported. This does not determine statutory injury-notice timing.

personal_injury.initial_reporting_method.value: Send written Medicaid injury-claim notification to HMS New York Casualty / Gainwell: nysubro@gainwelltechnologies.com; fax 877-476-9126; HMS Casualty Recovery Unit, PO Box 22053, Albany, NY 12201-2055. The preferred published phone remains available for intake assistance. This confirms the program notification branch, not formal lawsuit service or a successful file opening. The reviewer does not report NY matters online; the submissions portal is used for later existing-file requests.
personal_injury.initial_reporting_method.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. Published written reporting contacts retained; no SOLARIS or online case-opening method inferred.

personal_injury.form_name.value: HMS Case Information Form (CIF) plus signed authorization.
personal_injury.form_name.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. The reviewer uses the same opening package for PI and WC. A particular blank NY form URL was not supplied.

personal_injury.required_information.value: Submit the CIF plus signed authorization. The reviewer reports no difference between the PI and WC opening packages.
personal_injury.required_information.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. Opening documents only; NY WC settlement-specific requirements remain unconfirmed.

workflow.case_creation.value: Report through the established written NY route. The HMS case ID comes in initial correspondence by letter or fax; the reviewer does not report NY matters online.
workflow.case_creation.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. No immediate online case-ID issuance is asserted.

workflow.case_number_requirements.value: Obtain the HMS case ID from initial correspondence by letter or fax before using the existing-file submissions portal. Public entry pages also require member DOB and CAPTCHA.

workflow.document_submission.value: Opening package: CIF plus signed authorization, the same for PI and WC. Later documents are submitted through https://submissions.hms.com/submissions/documentUpload?ctx=CTSCASNY using the existing HMS case ID, member DOB and CAPTCHA.
workflow.document_submission.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. Accepted submission practice is distinct from formal NY WC settlement requirements.

workflow.initial_claim_request.value: Reporting the NY HMS injury matter triggers the initial lien; a separate initial request is not needed in the reviewer’s practice. No stated initial-lien timeframe was supplied.
workflow.initial_claim_request.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. No NJ 60-day statement imported.

workflow.interim_claim_request.value: Request updated/interim lien figures through the existing-file HMS submissions portal using the HMS case reference, following the same practical request approach the reviewer uses for NJ.
workflow.interim_claim_request.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. User confirms NY request practice; no NJ processing timeframe or tested portal-control inventory imported.

workflow.final_claim_request.value: Request the final lien figure through the existing-file HMS submissions portal using the HMS case reference, following the same practical request approach the reviewer uses for NJ.
workflow.final_claim_request.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. Final figure is case-specific. This does not establish NY WC settlement documents, clearance or approval requirements.

workflow.settlement_reporting.value: Accepted submission practice: the reviewer gives NY HMS the same package given to NJ HMS—gross settlement, attorney’s fee and costs; signed settlement statement for PI, proposed order for WC—and NY HMS accepts what is submitted. The reviewer cannot confirm what HMS specifically requests on a NY WC settlement. NY WC settlement requirements remain open. Separately, the published OMIG reduction process calls for a written request with settlement breakdown and other liens.
workflow.settlement_reporting.note: Practitioner-confirmed NY HMS experience only. Acceptance of the supplied package is confirmed experience, not a formal NY checklist or confirmation of WC settlement sufficiency.

workflow.payment.value: The supplied October 25, 2025 NY OMIG/HMS final-lien letter directs a check payable to New York State Department of Health, mailed to NEW YORK STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH, P.O. Box 415874, Boston, MA 02241-5874. Include the recipient’s name and recovery case number with payment. Follow the actual file’s current demand for the amount and current instructions.
workflow.payment.note: User-supplied dated correspondence, visually reviewed. No claim that this lockbox applies unchanged to every file. No formal NY WC settlement checklist inferred.

workflow.case_creation.value: After the prescribed notice, the Department’s rule requires written acknowledgment within 3 business days and an amount/itemized charge list within 15 business days. It also describes written confirmation of Medicaid/MCO status. This establishes acknowledgment behavior, not issuance of a particular recovery-number format.
workflow.case_creation.note: Saved COMAR .04E-G text. Rule timing is distinct from an observed response or a statement that every plan interest is resolved. The broad transaction hold retains its unestablished scope.

workflow.initial_claim_request.value: The prescribed departmental notice triggers the rule’s amount and itemized charge list within 15 business days; later provider charges can update the claim. This is the departmental notice/claims procedure, not a final-demand determination.
workflow.initial_claim_request.note: Saved COMAR .04E-G. Separate assignment/MCO scope and actual finality remain applicable.

workflow.settlement_reporting.value: The rule calls for additional written notice before resolution or within 30 calendar days after judgment/award as specified in .04C, and notice of the amount and terms of judgment, award or settlement within 30 calendar days under .04D.
workflow.settlement_reporting.note: Saved COMAR .04C-D; retain the exact rule and trigger. A complete attachment checklist or case-specific approval is not inferred.

personal_injury.initial_reporting_method.value: First identify which payer paid the injury-related claims. For MCO-paid claims, contact that plan’s subrogation office to open a case: WellSense TPL Unit: 617-748-6188 (option 2 in the 2019 notice); NH Healthy Families / Rawlings: 888-285-1276 (attorney line); AmeriHealth Caritas NH / Discovery Health Partners: 866-401-6061. For directly paid NH Medicaid (FFS) claims, use NH DHHS, Bureau of Program Integrity, TPL Unit, 129 Pleasant Street, Thayer Building, Concord NH 03301. The 2019 transition notice retains already-open DHHS cases with DHHS and sends new MCO cases to the MCO even for earlier accident/service dates.

User approved operational use on November 15, 2026. Phone contacts have newer corroboration; this is not a completed referral or confirmation of current menu/fax behavior. Use for NH Medicaid Accident and Trauma subrogation for claims the named plan paid, including workplace-accident inquiries. Existing FFS notice qualifications remain applicable.

The 2026 subrogation section explicitly gives this specialty-program number; do not substitute Home State Health’s other-plan number. The separate 800-877-6876 accident-questionnaire line is an existing-questionnaire contact, not this initial reporting route.

Identify separately paid HFS and other-plan interests; the HFS state recovery office is not blanket plan clearance. General plan inquiry routes: Use ABHILProviderRelations@aetna.com or 866-329-4701 to request plan-side assistance and the assigned casualty handler when no vendor file is known. The April 2026 notice supplies provider TPL assistance, not an express attorney casualty filing instruction. Optum is documented handling an Aetna Illinois lien in the cited court case;  its POBox 182643ColumbusOH 43218 is that record’s lien-payment address. Call 877-860-2837 for BCCHP plan/TPL inquiry and request routing for an injury-recovery matter. The published article concerns provider other-insurance validation and claim disputes;  it does not establish this as a dedicated casualty unit or confirm the parent 800-582-6418 line for Medicaid. Contact countycareproviderservices@cookcountyhhs.org or 312-864-8200,option 3, and request the CountyCare TPL/Finance recovery handler. The October 2026 guide confirms shared provider inquiry contacts;  attorney casualty service and a dedicated subrogation endpoint remain to be established. Do not equate CountyCare plan recovery with a CCH hospital lien. Call Meridian Medicaid 866-606-3700 to identify the assigned subrogation handler;  its official page directs legal matters to Attn:Legal,CentenePlaza,7700ForsythBoulevard,StLouisMO 63105. Rawlings and First Recovery Group are named in the Medicaid payment-code crosswalk;  the court record documents Meridian Medicaid liens with Equian/Rawlings. Confirm the current file’s handler rather than assigning all cases to one vendor. Use ILYouthCare@centene.com or 844-289-2264 for program-specific inquiry and request its casualty-recovery handler. Keep YouthCare identity separate from standard Meridian;  provider claim payerID instructions do not establish attorney notice requirements. DCFS.HealthPlan@illinois.gov/800-232-3798 is coverage/advocacy coordination, not a verified subrogation desk.
